claims.claim: The development of modern astrophysical science was made possible by abolishing the dichotomy between earth and sky and subjecting all earthly events to universally valid laws formulated from an Archimedean point.
qualifications: subject to a universally valid law valid beyond human sense experience, memory, organic life, and the earth herself
claims.supporting_excerpt: this development itself was possible only because at the beginning the old dichotomy between earth and sky was abolished and a unification of the universe effected, so that from then on nothing occurring in earthly nature was viewed as a mere earthly happening. All events were considered to be subject to a universally valid law in the fullest sense of the word... All laws of the new astrophysical science are formulated from the Archimedean point

claims.claim: Modern relativism originates conceptually from seventeenth-century theories by Galileo and Newton rather than directly from Einstein's theory of relativity.
qualifications: preceded by seventeenth-century theories according to which qualities like blue and heaviness are mere relations
claims.supporting_excerpt: The parentage of modern relativism is not in Einstein but in Galileo and Newton.

must_not_be_lost: Abolition of the earth-sky dichotomy and formulation of laws from the Archimedean point.
Transition from a heliocentric system to a centerless world view establishing humans as universal beings.
Fundamental role of earth alienation in modern natural science compared to other forms of alienation.
output.segment_function: Analyzing how the unification of the universe and the adoption of an Archimedean point enabled modern astrophysical science, universal relationalism, and fundamental earth alienation.
